angle: Executive sponsorship only works when it’s operationalized into a weekly cadence, shared metrics, and line ownership.
sourceTitle: GS Caltex’s Saehong Hur: Leading from the top; moving forward—together
linkedinPost:
Most AI programs don’t die from bad models. They die from weak leadership metabolism.

McKinsey’s interview with GS Caltex’s Saehong Hur underscores a simple truth: communication and an integrated mindset move organizations, not slogans. That’s the difference between pilots and production.

My take as a Forward Deployed Engineer: “executive sponsorship” only matters when it shows up on the calendar and the P&L. In the successful rollouts I’ve seen, leaders do three things:

1) Weekly operating cadence. A 30-minute forum where product, ops, data, and legal clear blockers fast.
2) Shared metrics. One scorecard tied to business outcomes (AHT, NPS, $/case), not vanity model stats.
3) Line ownership. AI outcomes sit with business leaders, not an innovation lab with no quota.

Bonus: public wins. Celebrate retired processes and measurable savings so teams believe change is real.

If your AI initiative vanished from the exec agenda last quarter, it’s already losing altitude. What’s the one ritual you’ll put in place next week to make leadership visible and useful? #AIStrategy #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI
